chunks: Hammad ibn Isa narrated from Muawiya ibn Wahb from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said: A man from your mawla, from their loyal followers, complained to me about what he experiences regarding sleep. He said: I intend to stand for night prayer, but sleep overcomes me until morning. Sometimes I make up my prayer for the entire consecutive month, and for two months I endure its heaviness. He (peace be upon him) said: 'A delight of the eye for him, by Allah, and He did not grant him permission to pray in the first part of the night.' And he said: 'Making up the prayer during the day is superior.' I said: Among our women, there are young girls who love goodness and its people, and are eager for prayer, but sleep overcomes them. Sometimes they make it up, and sometimes they become weak from making it up, while they strive to perform it in the first part of the night. So he granted them permission 'to pray in the first part of the night if they become weak and neglect making it up.'

key_terms.أَوَّلُ اللَّيْلِ: The first part of the night

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on making up missed night prayers if one falls asleep?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the general rule for men and the specific concession for women regarding night prayer (Qiyam al-Layl). He establishes that while making up missed night prayers during the day is superior for men who struggle with sleep, women who are eager for worship but become too weak to perform the makeup prayer are permitted to pray in the early night to preserve their spiritual enthusiasm.
